questions.subject: Percentages & Profit
questions.question: A price rises by 20% and then falls by 20%. What is the net change from the original price?
questions.explanation: Take the original price as 100. After the rise it is 120; after the fall it is 120 × 0.8 = 96. The net decrease is 4%.

questions.subject: Percentages & Profit
questions.question: After a 15% discount, a bag costs ₹1,020. What was its marked price?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 85% of the marked price. Marked price = 1,020 ÷ 0.85 = ₹1,200.

questions.subject: Percentages & Profit
questions.question: An article costing ₹800 is marked at ₹1,000 and sold at a 10% discount on the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1,000 × 0.9 = ₹900. Profit = 900 − 800 = ₹100. Profit percentage = 100 ÷ 800 × 100 = 12.5%.

questions.subject: Ratio & Average
questions.question: ₹840 is divided between A and B in the ratio 3 : 4. How much does B receive?
questions.explanation: There are 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts. Each part is 840 ÷ 7 = ₹120. B receives 4 × 120 = ₹480.

questions.subject: Ratio & Average
questions.question: The average of five numbers is 18. One number, 12, is replaced by 27. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Original sum = 5 × 18 = 90. New sum = 90 − 12 + 27 = 105. New average = 105 ÷ 5 = 21.

questions.subject: Time & Work
questions.question: A can complete a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together at their usual constant rates, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: Combined daily work = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the job. Required time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.subject: Time & Work
questions.question: A pipe fills an empty tank in 6 hours. A drain empties a full tank in 9 hours. With both open and constant rates, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net filling rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 1/18 tank per hour. The empty tank therefore fills in 18 hours.

questions.subject: Speed & Distance
questions.question: A cyclist travels 30 km at 15 km/h and returns along the same route at 10 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: The two trips take 30/15 = 2 hours and 30/10 = 3 hours. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 60/5 = 12 km/h.

questions.subject: Speed & Distance
questions.question: A train 180 m long travels at 54 km/h. How long does it take to pass a pole completely?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. To pass a pole, the train travels its own length. Time = 180/15 = 12 seconds.

questions.subject: Interest
questions.question: A sum earns ₹720 simple interest in 3 years at 8% per year. What is the principal?
questions.explanation: Simple interest = P × R × T / 100. Therefore P = 720 × 100 / (8 × 3) = ₹3,000.

questions.subject: Interest
questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹5,000 at 10% per year for 2 years, compounded annually?

questions.subject: Number System
questions.question: What is the least common multiple of 12, 18 and 30?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3; 18 = 2 × 3²; 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. Taking the highest power of each prime gives 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.

questions.subject: Number System
questions.question: Two ribbons are 84 cm and 126 cm long. They must be cut into equal-length pieces with no waste. What is the greatest possible length of each piece?
questions.explanation: The required length is the greatest common divisor of 84 and 126. Since 84 = 2 × 42 and 126 = 3 × 42, the greatest length is 42 cm.

questions.subject: Number System
questions.question: What is the remainder when 7 × 8 × 9 + 5 is divided by 7?
questions.explanation: The product 7 × 8 × 9 is divisible by 7. Adding 5 leaves remainder 5.

questions.subject: Ratio & Average
questions.question: A mother is three times as old as her daughter. After 10 years, the mother will be twice as old as her daughter. What is the daughter’s present age?
questions.explanation: Let the daughter’s age be x, so the mother is 3x. Then 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10), giving x = 10 years.

questions.subject: Mensuration
questions.question: A rectangle has perimeter 50 cm and length 15 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: 2(length + width) = 50, so width = 25 − 15 = 10 cm. Area = 15 × 10 = 150 cm².

questions.subject: Mensuration
questions.question: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Using π = 22/7, what is its volume?

questions.subject: Number System
questions.question: What is the value of 3/4 + 2/3 − 1/6?

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: A sequence starts at 4 and adds consecutive odd numbers 5, 7, 9, 11, and so on. What comes after 4, 9, 16, 25?
questions.explanation: The next increment after 5, 7 and 9 is 11. Therefore the next term is 25 + 11 = 36.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: In a code, each letter is replaced by the next letter of the English alphabet (Z becomes A). How is TRAIN written?
questions.explanation: Shift each letter forward once: T→U, R→S, A→B, I→J, N→O. The result is USBJO.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 6 km east and then 8 km north. What is the shortest straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: The two walks form perpendicular sides of a right triangle. Distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: Meena is 9th from the front and 14th from the back in a single queue. How many people are in the queue?
questions.explanation: Total = front rank + back rank − 1 = 9 + 14 − 1 = 22. Subtract one because Meena is included in both counts.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Which conclusion must follow from these statements?
options: None of the first three conclusions necessarily follows
questions.explanation: The flowers that fade quickly may include roses, or may all be other flowers. The statements do not determine whether any roses fade quickly, so none of the first three conclusions is guaranteed.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be 45 days from today?
questions.explanation: 45 = 6 × 7 + 3. Six complete weeks leave the weekday unchanged; three more days after Wednesday give Saturday.

questions.subject: Ratio & Average
questions.question: A shop sold 40 notebooks on Monday, 55 on Tuesday, 45 on Wednesday and 60 on Thursday. What was the average number sold per day over these four days?
questions.explanation: Total notebooks = 40 + 55 + 45 + 60 = 200. Average over four days = 200/4 = 50.
